page: Microsoft Azure E4-2as_v7 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance running on Microsoft Hyper-V. It is configured with a constrained core topology featuring 2 vCPUs across a single physical core with multithreading enabled. Compute is powered by an x86_64 AMD EPYC 9V45 processor clocked at up to 4.5 GHz, supported by 48 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of shared L3 cache. The instance includes hardware instruction support for AVX-512 (including VNNI and BF16), SHA-NI, and VAES.

The instance is equipped with 32.0 GB of system memory, providing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 16 GB per virtual core. It includes no local instance storage, requiring remote persistent disks for operating system and data requirements. There are also no bundled graphics processing units or complimentary public IPv4 addresses included with the instance.

Benchmark evaluation demonstrates exceptional single-core execution speed alongside multi-threaded throughput limitations. In single-threaded compression benchmarks, the AMD EPYC 9V45 architecture scores in the top tier, achieving 40.38 GB/sec in gzip compression and 17.5 GB/sec in bzip3 decompression, alongside top-tier stress-ng single-core performance. Conversely, aggregate multi-core metrics such as the PassMark CPU score (5069.68) and stress-ng multi-core fall into the lower quartile due to the two-vCPU hardware constraint. Large-block memory bandwidth benchmarks register in the middle tier, delivering 44.35 GB/sec for read operations and 33.96 GB/sec for write operations.

The hardware configuration provides high cost efficiency for workloads that require significant memory capacities per thread but do not demand wide horizontal parallelism. However, tasks bound by aggregate multithreaded compute or high web concurrency will experience bottlenecks. Microsoft Azure E4-2as_v7 is primarily suited for mid-sized in-memory caching layers, single-node transactional databases with low thread counts, memory-heavy background batch processing, and lightweight machine learning inference pipelines.

The CPU features modern instruction sets including AVX-512 and VAES, though the instance includes no local storage or GPUs. Benchmark testing reveals top-tier single-threaded capability, achieving 40.38 GB/sec in gzip compression and strong single-core stress-ng scores. However, overall multi-core performance is naturally constrained by the dual-vCPU ceiling, placing aggregate throughput benchmarks like PassMark CPU in the lower quartile.
